He is in much better shape than he thinks. Ignoring cash and crypto, their 440k would pass 1.5 million in current dollars by 60 at 5 percent real growth with nothing added. Normal retirement is roughly covered, and retiring in their early 50s is realistic if they keep investing.

The real risk is concentration. Crypto is a third of their portfolio, likely mostly one coin, and both incomes face the same AI threat. House money needed within a year should not sit in something that can halve in weeks, so cashing out enough for the down payment into the HYSA or Treasury bills would lock in the win. Long term gains cost roughly 15 to 19 percent federal plus state at their income.

Buying the next house while both still work makes approval easier, but the payment should work on his 150k alone. If it only works on two incomes, the plan breaks the moment either job goes. Moving before baby two avoids a rushed purchase, and 6 to 12 months of expenses should stay in cash after closing. Renting out the current place only makes sense if rent clearly beats the 1700 payment plus upkeep.

His wife stepping back costs less than it seems, since after taxes and daycare for two kids her net could be under half her salary. Part time work or consulting instead of quitting keeps her skills current, a hedge if his job goes first.

They send 3200 a month to a taxable brokerage while barely passing the 401k match, yet each pretax 401k dollar saves at least 22 percent in federal tax. After the match, the usual order is HSA if eligible, Roth IRAs for both, via backdoor if over the income limit, then max both 401ks, then the brokerage. Add a 529 for the kids.

Term life on both, disability insurance for him, and wills naming a guardian should come before either big change. Not financial advice. A fee only planner could stress test the one income plan.
